long_biography.plain_text:
At seventeen, Elías Cababie Daniel joined a garment manufacturer operated by his family. Mexico's opening to imported goods changed that sector's prospects. Elías, Abraham and Jacobo responded by establishing a property enterprise that became GICSA. Elías oversaw the board, while Abraham directed management. The company grew from an early Mexico City building into commercial, residential, office, industrial and hospitality developments.

Elías continues to oversee GICSA's board and executive strategy. Together with Abraham and immediate relatives, he belongs to the issuer's controlling ownership bloc. That founder equity keeps his identifiable interests centered on property, although the textile business supplied a valuable starting platform. His personal connection is through his stake in the developer. The corporate estate, construction budgets, borrowings, revenue and wider family's combined shares cannot be assigned to him individually.
